Fig. 1. Illustration of the comparison of different image segmentation methods on the image from the dataset [18]. The segmentation results (red lines) from the asymmetric geodesic voting model [19], the min-cut Randers model [20] and the proposed MPV model are exhibited in figures a to c, respectively. The yellow dots indicate the landmark points inside the target region and the blue lines depict the adaptive domain cut [21].

Fig. 4. Illustration of the contour evolution process for extracting the circular min-cut geodesic path. (a) Initialization using a circular geodesic path (green line) derived from the orientation-constrained domain cut (blue line). The cyan point marks the landmark position, and the magenta point indicates the specified vertex. (b) Intermediate contour evolution steps (white lines) from the initial contour (green line) to the final segmentation result (red line). (c) Enlarged view of the subregion highlighted by the cyan rectangle in Figure b. The image is from the dataset [33].
